theme: 3 terms on what an app is allowed to do: the feature you switch on in Xcode, the signed key that grants it, and the walls that keep every app in its own space

terms.definition: A feature like push notifications or App Groups that you switch on for a target in Xcode.
terms.example: Turn on the Push Notifications Capability before you test remote notifications.

terms.definition: A key signed into your app that grants it a specific permission, like using an App Group.
terms.example: The build won't install because the profile doesn't include that Entitlement.

terms.definition: The walls around each app that limit which files and system resources it can reach.
terms.example: The App Sandbox blocks other apps' files, so share through an App Group.

quizzes.question: What keeps each app inside its own files and resources?
What signed key grants an app one specific permission?
What do you switch on for a target in Xcode, like Push Notifications?

video.title: Capability, Entitlement & App Sandbox | Day 91
video.description:
Learn to explain what an iOS app is allowed to do: Capability, Entitlement & App Sandbox, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Capability - A feature like push notifications or App Groups that you switch on for a target in Xcode.
Entitlement - A key signed into your app that grants it a specific permission, like using an App Group.
App Sandbox - The walls around each app that limit which files and system resources it can reach.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Capability, Entitlement & App Sandbox in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

Capability - A feature like push notifications or App Groups that you switch on for a target in Xcode.
한국어: 캐퍼빌리티: 푸시 알림이나 App Groups처럼 Xcode에서 타깃별로 켜는 기능

Entitlement - A key signed into your app that grants it a specific permission, like using an App Group.

App Sandbox - The walls around each app that limit which files and system resources it can reach.
한국어: 앱 샌드박스: 각 앱이 접근할 수 있는 파일과 시스템 자원을 제한하는 울타리

landscape.hook: Same code, but it crashes only in the widget. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why only the widget?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the widget crashes, but the same code works in the app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It force unwraps the group container. That's `nil` in the widget.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why would it be nil there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The App Sandbox keeps each target in its own space.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The app has the App Groups Capability. Isn't that enough?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only for the app. The widget target needs the same Capability.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does turning it on actually change?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Xcode adds an Entitlement listing the group name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So without that Entitlement, the App Sandbox blocks the shared folder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. And check the group name matches in both targets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Same Capability, same Entitlement, then the widget can read the file.
The widget is a separate target, give it the same Capability.
